brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource Team: How to Activate a New Accounting Firm

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the License Service in the ESource system?
choices: To store client names, bank statements, and transactions
To send sign-in codes, enforce plan limits, keep book counts, and issue keys to unlock books
To manage the firm's website and brand colors
To process monthly billing payments from client accounts
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the License Service is the backbone that handles authentication and access control while protecting client data.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The License Service does not store sensitive client data or process payments. It focuses on authentication, access control, and usage tracking.

questions.question: What is a Firm ID and what are its key constraints?
choices: The firm's legal name, which can include spaces and uppercase letters
A short, lowercase identifier with no spaces that never changes once chosen
The firm's web address, such as smithco.esourcebookkeeper.com
The tier level assigned to the firm, such as 'Pro' or 'Enterprise'
questions.feedback_correct: You've got it—the Firm ID is permanent and must follow strict formatting rules to work properly in the system.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A Firm ID is a technical identifier, not the firm's legal name or web address. It must be short, lowercase, with no spaces, and it cannot be changed later.

questions.question: What are the four things that must be in place before activating a firm?
choices: Signed agreement, plan tier agreed in writing, security plan and lead named, and firm details collected
Firm's web address, owner email, logo file, and payment method on file
Admin page access, Vercel account, Cloudflare settings, and staff member list
Monthly billing preferences, help assistant settings, reminder configuration, and storage key
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—these four prerequisites ensure legal compliance, clear expectations, and readiness before any technical setup begins.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While the other items are part of activation, the four prerequisites are the agreement, tier confirmation, security documentation with a named lead, and the firm's basic information.

questions.question: In Step 3, when adding a domain in Cloudflare DNS Records, what must the proxy cloud setting be and why?
choices: Orange, because it enhances Vercel's security certificate
Blue, to match Vercel's checkmark status
Gray, meaning DNS only, because an orange cloud blocks Vercel's security certificate
Red, to prevent unauthorized access to the domain
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—this is a critical detail that ensures the security certificate works correctly with Vercel.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The proxy cloud must be set to gray (DNS only), not orange. An orange cloud will actually block Vercel's security certificate from functioning properly.

questions.question: How does the monthly billing calculation work in the system?
choices: Bill based on the total number of client books ever added to the firm's account
Bill from the 'Highest by month' number using the tier rates, where the rate depends on the total count of active books on any single day that month
Bill a flat rate per staff member multiplied by the tier level
Bill based on the number of sign-ins and hours the firm used the system
questions.feedback_correct: You understand the billing model—it's based on peak usage in a month, not total usage or static rates.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Billing is based on the peak number of active books on any single day in the month, using tiered rates that decrease as the book count increases. The 'Ever added' count is tracked separately.

questions.question: What happens when a firm's plan is full and a staff member tries to add a new client book?
choices: The system automatically upgrades the firm to the next tier
An error message appears, and this is an opportunity to offer the next tier
The request is queued and processed at the end of the business day
The new client book is created but marked as inactive until payment is received
questions.feedback_correct: Right—a full plan is a natural moment to discuss upgrading to a higher tier with more book capacity.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When a plan is full, the user cannot add a client. This is not an automatic upgrade but a support moment to discuss moving to a higher tier.

questions.question: What is the difference between the 'name' and 'firm' settings in the firm's profile block in profiles.js?
choices: 'Name' is the Firm ID and 'firm' is the web address
'Name' shows at the top of the screen and 'firm' is the name clients see on reports and Excel sheets
'Name' is the owner's name and 'firm' is the legal business name
'Name' is used for internal tracking and 'firm' is used only for billing purposes
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—these settings control two different user-facing displays: one for internal staff and one for external client communication.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The 'name' setting displays at the top of the internal screen, while 'firm' appears on client-facing documents like statement requests and Excel report headers.

questions.question: If a firm uses its own domain instead of a subdomain, what additional step must be taken to ensure the help assistant works on their site?
choices: The firm's domain must be registered with Vercel as an additional project
The firm's domain must be added to the assistant's allowed websites in ElevenLabs
The firm must purchase a separate license for the help assistant feature
The firm's owner must manually enable the assistant in their profile settings
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—this is an important configuration step when firms use their own domain rather than our subdomain.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When a firm uses its own domain, the help assistant's allowed websites list in ElevenLabs must be updated. This is necessary because the assistant security check validates the domain before allowing the help button to work.

questions.question: Based on the course's explanation of how the system works, why is it significant that 'the same program serves every firm'?
choices: It reduces costs because ESource only needs to maintain one codebase rather than multiple versions
It ensures that a fix made once automatically reaches every firm, providing consistent quality across all clients
It allows firms to share client books across their organization
It prevents firms from customizing their profiles or branding
questions.feedback_correct: You've identified the core operational benefit—a single shared application means efficiency and consistency across the entire customer base.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While cost efficiency is a benefit, the primary significance highlighted in the course is that one shared program means any fix is automatically deployed to every firm, ensuring consistent quality.

questions.question: Why does the system lock a computer after fourteen days without internet, and what is the user's action to regain access?
choices: To prevent unauthorized access; the user must contact support and provide identification
To save battery; the user must restart the computer and re-sign in
For safety; the user simply connects to the internet and signs in again
To enforce license renewal; the user must pay the monthly fee before accessing books
questions.feedback_correct: Right—this is a security measure that is self-resolving once connectivity is restored and the user authenticates.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The fourteen-day lockout is a safety feature to protect encrypted books. The resolution is straightforward: the user connects to the internet and signs in again.
